text: Refactoring is the process of improving the structure of your code without changing what it does. Think of it like cleaning a messy room: the furniture stays the same, but everything becomes easier to find and use. The main goal is readability, making sure that another developer (or your future self) can quickly understand the logic. This practice directly addresses technical debt, which is the extra work that piles up when you take shortcuts. By regularly refactoring, you remove confusing names, break long functions into smaller ones, and eliminate duplication. The result is cleaner, more maintainable software. Remember, refactoring is not about adding new features; it is about making the existing code better and safer for future changes.
